description: ENERTALK provides whole-house and appliance-level electricity observations from 22 houses in Korea. Its research team publishes active and reactive power at 15 Hz, with millisecond timestamps, as daily Parquet files grouped into house-specific ZIP deposits. Figshare hosts the complete collection and all 22 inspected house records state CC0, allowing free reuse. Exact recording periods and appliance availability vary across houses and should be checked before constructing a common sample. The companion ENERTALK-dataset GitHub repository contains plotting notebooks, a NILMTK converter and a metadata generator; its software licence was not established from the inspected README or API metadata. The observations can calibrate appliance-demand and energy-disaggregation models for building simulations, complementing data-uk-dale-domestic-appliance-level-electricity. A caveat is that gaps and unequal observation coverage require explicit treatment, as illustrated by the provider's gap and observation-ratio notebooks. The data licence should not be assumed to license the companion software. No household data files or code environment were downloaded or run.
